# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We as members, contributors, and maintainers pledge to make participation in the Lumastra
community a harassment-free and welcoming experience for everyone, regardless of
age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality,
personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse,
inclusive, and healthy community.

## Our standard

This project adopts the **[Contributor Covenant, version 2.1](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/)**
as its code of conduct. Please read it in full at the link above. In short:

- Be respectful, considerate, and collaborative.
- Assume good faith and offer constructive feedback.
- Behavior that is harassing, demeaning, or otherwise unwelcoming is not tolerated.

Maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing these standards and may take
appropriate, fair corrective action in response to behavior they deem inappropriate.

## Content rules

These apply to issues, pull requests, discussions and every other project space, in
addition to the standard above.

- **No piracy, not even a hint of it.** Lumastra is a media server for content you own or
  are licensed to use. Do not post, link to, or allude to pirated content in any form: no
  indexers, trackers, release groups, IPTV playlists or Xtream providers without a licence,
  or "where do I get…"; no filenames, paths, screenshots
  or logs that reveal unlicensed copies (redact them before posting; `movie.mkv` is
  enough); no requests to make Lumastra work with any of that. Integrations that Lumastra
  ships (Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr) are fine to discuss as features; what those tools fetch
  from is not a topic here. Posts that break this rule are removed without discussion, and
  repeat offenders are banned.
- **No personal instance or library showcases.** Do not post galleries of your media
  collection or instance. Screenshots needed to explain a bug, documentation issue or
  contribution must use generic test media and contain no piracy references, secrets or
  personal data.
- **Security reports go through the private reporting process**, never a public issue,
  discussion or Discord channel. See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Sapd/lumastra/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md).
- **Reports and PRs must be verified by a human.** Unverified AI-generated bug reports,
  security reports and PRs are closed. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Sapd/lumastra/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- **No contribution farming, no taking other people's work.** Opening PRs just to have
  opened them, and submitting code, translations or other work copied from someone else
  without the right to do so, get the author banned without warning.
- **Stay on topic.** Discord help channels are for informal troubleshooting, with one thread
  per question. Lasting support questions and answers belong in the matching GitHub
  Discussions category; bugs in issues; features in the Features category. Maintainers move or
  close posts that land in the wrong place.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces (issues, pull requests, discussions,
Discord and any other project channels) and also applies when an individual is officially representing
the project in public spaces.

## Reporting

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the
project maintainer at **<git@sapd.eu>**. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated
promptly and fairly. Maintainers are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the
reporter of any incident.

## Enforcement guidelines

Maintainers will follow the Contributor Covenant's
[Enforcement Guidelines](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/#enforcement-guidelines)
when determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of
Conduct. The exception: contribution farming and taking other people's work lead straight
to a permanent ban, without the warning steps.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org),
version 2.1.
